notes: Step 1 parts are unchanged. The USB cable is not in the parts list, so it is not included.

Breadboard naming: the catalogue calls the top half bank 't' with rows a-e. The image labels its upper half f-j and its lower half a-e. I used the image's row letters and mapped rows a-e to bank 't', so the lower half of the drawing is 't' and the rails beside it are tp (+) and tn (-). Only strip membership matters electrically.
Button straddles the centre gap in columns 6 and 8. Side 1 (1.l, 1.r) is column 6, which carries pin 4 and the resistor. Side 2 (2.l, 2.r) is column 8, which goes to the 5V rail.
Rail hole numbers (tp.3, tp.7, tn.2, tn.5) are approximate. Each rail is a single strip, so the exact hole does not change the circuit.

The blue wire goes from Leonardo pin 4 to column 6, and the 10k resistor runs from column 6 to the GND rail, so it works as a pull-down. The manual text says pin 4, but the schematic labels it pin 2; I followed the text and the circuit image.
The Leonardo's 5V and GND header pins are used as ports. The black wire goes to GND.1.
